title: Rollout ops speed-dial + observability runbook (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick-reference ops runbook for small-to-medium rollouts (cohorts of up to 10% traffic). Focused on speed-dial actions + minimal observability sampling to make go/no-go decisions in the first 30 minutes.

Audience:
- Release owners, on-call SRE, release shepherd, product PM on watch
- Assumes release is already through staging gates and has basic smoke tests green

High-level cadence (0 -> 120 minutes):
- T-0 (traffic flip begins): shift 1% -> observe 5 min
- T+5m: decide rapid expand to 5% or hold/rollback
- T+20m: expand to 25% if signals OK
- T+60m: expand to 50% if steady; otherwise hold and run diagnostics
- T+120m: finish rollout or execute rollback plan

Quick signals (speed-dial):
- Latency P95 (api.response.time.p95): threshold 400ms baseline + 40% increase = abort
- Error count (http.5xx, inference.error.rate): > +200 absolute or > 3x baseline in 5m -> stop and investigate
- Token cost spike (billing.per_token_usd.rate): +25% -> investigate model variant or batching config
- KV cache miss ratio (kv.cache.miss.pct): > 20% -> expect latency impact; consider throttling slow cohort

Sampling plan (observability-lite):
- First 10 minutes: sample 100% of requests for latency and 5xx tagging, retain full traces for 1% of requests (trace-sampler=1.0 for trace-ids matching cohort)
- First 60 minutes: reduce full-trace sampling to 0.1% except for flagged requests with errors
- Always capture prompt/response length histogram and kv-cache hit/miss for the cohort
- Nightlights: if rollout overlaps a regional night window, double sampling for the first 15 minutes

Runbook checklists (pre-deploy):
- [ ] Canary image built and artifact hash pinned in release manifest (manifest:models.json:hash)
- [ ] Preflight smoke (end-to-end sample prompts) x3 in target region: PASS
- [ ] Circuit-breaker thresholds configured for new model variant
- [ ] Canary alert group created: #release-watch + pager rotation assigned
- [ ] Observe-config applied: trace-sample rules + cohort tag (tag:rollout=cohort-A)
- [ ] Fallback mapping present (route to smaller model or last-known-good) and tested

Day-of ops commands (speed-dial snippets):
- Increase cohort backoff: curl -XPOST https://ops-api/rollout/cohort/adjust -d '{"cohort":"A","backoff_pct":50}' 
- Force-fallback: curl -XPOST https://ops-api/fallback/trigger -d '{"target":"last-known-good"}'
- Kill misbehaving worker: kubectl -n inference delete pod <pod-name> --grace-period=0

Telemetry triage flow (first 15 minutes):
1) Triage latency spike -> check worker GC, quantization fallback logs, kernel selection logs (runtime.kernels.log).
2) If 5xx spike -> fetch sample traces (trace ids where status >=500), check model cache warming errors and tokenization failures.
3) If cost spike -> check batch size distribution and model version mapped to request.

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Any sustained P95 > baseline * 1.4 for 10+ minutes AND increasing error rate
- New critical customer impacting errors (JIRA-sev1 opened)
- Observed drift in generation quality metrics tied to eval set (quality.regression > 5 points)

Rollback playbook (fast):
- Immediate: set route weight to 0 for cohort in router (ops-api) + enable last-known-good fallback
- Notify: @release-owner, @oncall-sre, #release-ops channel with short list of observations and top 3 traces attached
- Postmortem starter: create JIRA ticket with template: release-rollback-<date>-<release-id> and attach logs/traces

Annotated release notes (draft to push to GitHub release):
- Release name: rollout/2026-08/telemetry-speed-dial
- Owner: Emily Chen
- Summary: Emergency-speed-dial observability controls + sampling defaults for faster rollouts. Adds cohort tagging and fast fallback mappings.
- Notable changes:
  * Default trace sampling increased to 1% for new rollouts, cohort-tagging introduced (rollout=cohort-A).
  * Ops API endpoints to nudge cohort backoff and force fallback (PR #8124).
  * Two new alerts: latency-p95-surge and model-cache-eviction-rate.
- Known issues / caveats:
  * Trace retention for sampled traces is limited to 7 days (for now).
  * Some third-party quantized kernels log at DEBUG level and may need logfiltering; this creates noise in early minutes.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we make the sampling rules per-tenant rather than global? tradeoffs: cost vs. signal fidelity.
- Add synthetic traffic generator that hits worst-case prompt lengths during first 2 minutes. (ticket JIRA-4599)
- Confirm legal/PII constraints on storing prompt text in traces for customer cohorts; file with security if needed.

Post-roll checklist (30m after full rollout):
- [ ] Confirm steady-state P95 within +10% of baseline for 1 hour
- [ ] Check cost curve vs expected unit economics for the new model variant
- [ ] Flip off extra trace-sampling rules to default level
- [ ] Create short release digest and post to #product-releases and confluence page

Notes: keep this doc lean; intended as a speed-dial card for on-call and release shepherds. We'll spin a more formal playbook if this pattern repeats 3x in the next quarter.

Slack shortcuts / channels referenced:
- #release-ops (primary watch)
- #sre-oncall (pager alerts)
- /rollout nudge <cohort> (internal bot)

Last edits: Emily Chen (2026-08-16) - tightened latency thresholds, added explicit sampling plan.

---
Raw scratch area (choppy):
- quick note: for night windows lower expansion ramp to 10% at T+20m.
- if KV miss high -> warm cache by replaying top 100 recent keys to warm layer.
- check PR 8124 for ops-api endpoint shapes
- TODO: small visual for 'watchlist' signals (P95, 5xx, cost, kv-miss).
